title: Introduction
content:
In today’s world, it’s common for every ache and ailment to
be tackled with a pill, a capsule, or a prescription, and as such,
it’s easy to forget that true healing often begins long before
we visit the pharmacy or consume any tablet. This book is an
invitation to rediscover the profound and often overlooked
power of the natural, emotional, and the spiritual in
maintaining and restoring health.
As a medical doctor with over 30 years of practice under my
belt, I can tell you for a fact that pharmaceutical drugs cannot
cure everything and taking them continuously all the time
doesn’t guarantee good health. Throughout my years of
experience, I've encountered different people with problems
that didn’t necessarily need a prescription, and in my quest to
help them and every other person around achieve and
maintain a healthy life, I went in search of knowledge beyond
medical school.
All the information in this book is tested and trusted, and no
one who has taken the information embedded in this book
seriously has ever given negative feedback or come back to

say they didn’t see significant changes and improvement in
their conditions.
Of course, it is true that not everything that works for Mr A
will work for Mrs B, but I can assure you that no matter who
you are, within these pages you will find some invaluable
information that will help you improve your overall health.
In Medicine Without Medication, we’re exploring the simple yet
very powerful truth that good health is not only the absence
of disease, but a state of physical, emotional, and spiritual
balance, and that reaching this state doesn’t always require
pharmaceutical intervention.
In this book, I’ll show you the remarkable healing properties
of everyday vegetables and plants in the chapter titled
Vegetables and Plants (God’s Pharmacy). This chapter will
reveal how natural foods can nourish, protect, and even
restore your body. You’ll learn how cinnamon, figs, barley,
pomegranates, olive oil, and more have supported human
health for centuries right from the days of the first man and
woman, long before modern medicine caught up.
In another chapter, Love: The Greatest of Them All, we’ll
explore the surprising scientificlink between emotional
wellbeing and physical health, including how love, joy,
connection, and community play essential roles in healing
and longevity.

Having dealt with a lot of pregnant women including my wife
and daughters, and being an elderly man myself at the time
of the writing and publishing of this book, I will be sharing
with us in the chapter titled Food for the Pregnant and Elderly
how targeted nutrition and lifestyle choices can support
these most vulnerable and vital stages of life.
Finally, every young person will get the nuggets they need in
the chapter General Health and Body Maintenance Without
Pharmaceutical Products. Here, we’ll bring it all together with
practical strategies for living a lifestyle that prevents illness,
builds resilience, and strengthens your body’s natural ability
to heal.
So, whether you are a young person seeking to build a strong
foundation, an expectant mother or supportive partner, or
someone entering the golden years of life, this book offers
timeless principles and modern insights to help you thrive
without always reaching for the pill bottles.
I need to state here though, that this isn’t a rejection of
modern medicine. I have been a medical doctor myself and I
know the benefits of modern medicine; and this book is a call
to reclaim your role in your own health story. Now let’s
explore together what it truly means to live well.

I want to begin this chapter by saying something I always like to say, 'Good health is part of God's plan for us, it is in the package that he came to deliver to us.'
I say this to the people I encounter as a doctor and as a child of God. I have been a doctor for over 30 years and back then when I read medicine, doctors handled every type of case. It wasn't like it is today where we have doctors having specialties or focusing on a particular aspect of medicine. I had to meet and treat all kinds of cases, from pregnant women, to sick children, to the elderly, to young people with different health challenges.
It was my desire to see people get better and stay healthy and so with the help and guidance of God, I spent years seeking for answers. You see, just as there were no specialties, so it was with the fact that there were lots of things medicine hadn't found the cure to, some breakthroughs concerning some illnesses hadn't been made, and yet people would come to us to help them find solutions to these health problems. Anyone who is a doctor or nurse passionate about saving lives can explain better how heartbreaking it feels to watch

people suffer without knowing what exactly to do to help them recover.
After medical school, and practicing for a few years, I travelled to different places including the East Coast of the United States, and then crossed over to the West Coast where I attended the Fuller Theological Seminary in California. There I met professors who, when I told them why I was there and the answers I was seeking, laughed at me and told me I was doing good already and that the possibility of getting what I was searching for was far-fetched.
I was searching for knowledge beyond medicine that I could share with people. I knew medicine was limited so I was searching for something greater and I found it. I met people who opened my eyes to certain age-long truths, and I discovered that living in good health was not only possible but easy and very doable.
Before I started sharing this information with my patients, I tried it on myself and my family. Things as simple as food, eating balanced diets, and paying attention to certain lifestyles and routines. As a young person I tried them on myself, as a pregnant woman I encouraged my wife to do them and we watched how many of these things positively influenced the development of our children.

I make bold to say that throughout my practice as a doctor, no pregnant woman who has been my patient has ever lost her life or her pregnancy. Every pregnant woman who has come to see me and adhered to my advice on what to do physically, mentally, and spiritually has always come back with good news of a healthy pregnancy and a healthy child.
In addition to pregnant women, the elderly testify to being healthier and stronger after following my advice. Personally, as an 80-year-old man, it is very hard for people to believe my age because nothing about me indicates that I’m that old. My skin has been complimented several times, and people cannot believe that an 80-year-old man can be this agile and healthy.
From the next chapter, I will begin to share the information you need to achieve these outcomes. Note that you don’t have to try everything or anything if you don’t want to, but if you desire good health, you might want to give it a thought. If you’re unsure about certain things, you can consult with your doctor to get his opinions and I’m sure he will counsel you accordingly.

In this chapter we’ll explore the transformative potential of exercise, which not only strengthens the body but also invigorates the mind and spirit.
We’ll also reintroduce fasting, not as deprivation, but as a time-honored practice that can rejuvenate cellular functions and enhance longevity.
We’ll talk about natural food, often overshadowed by processed alternatives, highlighting the nutritional powerhouses found in vegetables and whole foods that fuel our vitality, and we’ll look at the simple acts of laughter, sleep, forgiveness, and love, all universal yet frequently neglected, despite being foundational pillars of health, offering restorative benefits that no pill can replicate.

By weaving these elements together, Medicine Without Medication will be a guide to a lifestyle that honors the body’s natural rhythms and capabilities, and encourages you to cultivate a life of balance and wellness.
Let’s begin.
THE POWER OF EXERCISE
Research, along with my personal experience both as a medical doctor and an agile man, has proven that exercises like walking help with the stimulation of blood vessels. Half of the blood vessels found in the body are located from the hip downwards, so when you walk, you stimulate those blood vessels.
Aerobics, heart-pumping exercises that make you breathe hard, have also been found to be an effective way to open up blood vessels, mobilize the joints, help circulate food nutrients into places in the body they might have difficulty entering, and produce ketones which are food or fuel for the brain.

title: MEDICINE WITHOUT MEDICATION
content:
Exercise is not just about losing weight or building muscles;
it is a vital component of overall health. Regular physical
activities boost our mood, strengthen our hearts, and
improve our immune system. Whether it’s a brisk walk, a
dance class, or yoga, finding an activity you enjoy can make
all the difference.
So here’s what you need to do: Aim for at least 30 minutes of
movement for a minimum of three days of each week (the
WHO standard is 150 minutes weekly), and watch how it
transforms your energy levels and mental clarity.
THE BENEFITS OF FASTING
There is a large body of research that supports the benefits of
fasting, and fasting has been shown to improve biomarkers
of diseases, reduce oxidative stress, and preserve learning
and memory functioning.
Fasting has actually been in practice for centuries and is
gaining recognition for its health benefits. Intermittent
fasting has been practiced for decades even though it’s only
beginning to gain recognition for its health benefits.
Intermittent fasting can help regulate blood sugar levels,

promote weight loss, which is what most people are using it for now, and even enhance brain function.
How this works is that when you give your body a break from constant digestion and all the work that comes with it, you allow your body to focus on repair and rejuvenation. There are a lot of different approaches to intermittent fasting, some of which are the 16:8 method, the 5:2 diet, alternate day fasting, and the eat-stop-eat method.
What I’d advise you to do as a beginner to this method of fasting is to start with the simple method of skipping breakfast, I promise you will not die, see how your body responds to it, and then modify as you desire.
EMBRACING NATURAL FOOD
I’m pretty sure we all know at this point that what we eat plays a crucial role in our health, so making a choice to eat whole unprocessed foods like fruits, vegetables, nuts, and grains goes a long way in helping our bodies and our immune system get the support and nourishment they require to stay active and healthy. These foods that I mentioned above are packed with vitamins and antioxidants that help fight diseases.
Now here’s what you must do, if you’re honest with yourself and you know that your consumption of processed and

packaged food outweighs your intake of natural food, I advise that you make it a goal from now on to fill your plate with colorful vegetables and fruits. You can start with planning your weekly meals to accommodate natural food at least 3 times a week. Do this and notice the difference in how you feel.
THE HEALING POWER OF LAUGHTER
A lot of people tend to see smiling and laughing as simple, insignificant things we do that go unnoticed in our everyday lives, but the truth is that smiles and laughter have more implications than we know. Studies have shown that there are numerous benefits of both smiles and laughter, including boosting our mental and physical health, improving our social lives, and even increasing our lifespans.
You see, there are three hormones that make you feel good when you smile, and they are dopamine, endorphins, and serotonin. These hormones signal to your body that you are happy, and in turn you feel happier.
If you need any more convincing that the saying 'laughter is the best medicine' isn't just an empty saying, I can tell you that laughter reduces stress, boosts mood, and even strengthens the immune system. According to a 15-year-old Norwegian study, women with a strong sense of humor lived longer than others, and these women were 73% less likely to

die from heart disease, and 83% less likely to die from infection. Men with a better sense of humor seemed to be more protected from infection only, with a 74% less risk of death associated with high scores in humor.
Laughter stimulates organs. It can enhance your oxygen intake, stimulate your heart and other muscles, and decrease your heart rate and blood pressure. So do well to surround yourself with people who make you laugh, watch funny movies, or read a humorous book if you’re not the type that likes movies. Incorporating more laughter into your life will lead to a more positive outlook and improved health. As I always say, 'one of the secrets to staying healthy is to laugh a lot.'
THE IMPORTANCE OF SLEEP
Never underestimate the power of a good night’s sleep. Research has linked sleep to several brain functions including memory, performance, and cognition.
A 2015 study in the Journal of Child Psychology and Psychiatry showed that children’s sleep patterns could directly impact their behavior and academic performance, while a 2018 study suggests that people who regularly sleep less than seven hours a night are more likely to have a higher body mass index, BMI, and develop obesity than those who sleep more.

title: MEDICINE WITHOUT MEDICATION
content:
I could go on and on sharing different research on the
benefits of sleep and it all points to one thing: Sleep is
important for maintaining optimal health and well-being.
Like exercise and a balanced diet, getting enough sleep may
help prevent a range of health issues, including heart disease
and depression. Quality sleep is essential for both physical
and mental health, affecting everything from mood to
immune function.
Now, I understand that sleep needs vary from person to
person, depending on the individual’s age. As a person ages,
they require less sleep to function properly.
So below is a breakdown of the ideal number of sleep hours
every age group is supposed to have.
According to the CDC,
● Newborns (0–3 months): 14–17 hours
● Infants (4–12 months): 12–16 hours
● Toddler (1–2 years): 11–14 hours
● Preschool (3–5 years): 10–13 hours
● School age (6–12 years): 9–12 hours
● Teen (13–18 years): 8–10 hours
● Adult (18–60 years): 7-plus hours
● Adult (61–64 years): 7–9 hours
● Adult (65+ years): 7–8 hours

title: MEDICINE WITHOUT MEDICATION
content:
Finally, creating a calming bedtime routine, limiting screen
time before bed both for children and adults, and making
your sleep environment as comfortable as possible are great
ways to help you and your loved ones get a good and sound
sleep. In the chapter that talks about general health tips and
supplements, you’ll also find some natural sleep aids that can
help you have very sound sleep especially if you’re someone
who has difficulty falling asleep or if you’re a really light
sleeper and would love to change that.
SOAKING UP SUNLIGHT
Sunlight is a natural source of vitamin D (if you didn't already
know that), and Vitamin D is crucial for bone health and
immune function.
Spending time outdoors each day, whether it's on your street,
in a park, or walking to and from a nearby market or grocery
store instead of driving or taking a cab can be of great benefit
to you. Just be sure though to protect your skin from
overexposure and endeavor to use sunscreen. The optimal
time to soak up all the Vitamin D that the sun has for you is
between 7-9am in the morning. Plan your walks within that
time frame to maximize the benefits and to boost your
immune system.

A little sunlight can actually go a long way in boosting your mood and overall health, but do not overdo it. Don't trek for long distances under the scorching sun, and use sunscreen whenever you are going to spend a lot of time under the sun.
LIVING IN LOVE AND BEING LOVED
One of God’s gifts to us is human connection. It is something that is very vital for our well-being, so learning to cultivate relationships filled with love and support can greatly enhance our emotional health, which in turn impacts our physical health.
You don’t have to do anything out of the ordinary to achieve this, just doing things as simple as making time for your family and friends, expressing your love openly, and nurturing the good and positive connections, and doing all of these consistently can help you in no small way. This is because these connections fuel us in ways that we don’t even realize. Feeling loved and giving love impacts your overall happiness.
EATING VEGETABLES
Vegetables are God’s pharmacy. I have a whole chapter dedicated to that statement because, over the years, humans have lost the understanding of how vital eating plants and

title: MEDICINE WITHOUT MEDICATION
content:
vegetables is to our health. The goodness found in plants and
vegetables are so numerous and I explain them in-depth in
the next chapter.
Vegetables are rich in vitamins,
minerals, antioxidants, and
fiber. They support every
system in the body from
digestion to immunity to
mental clarity!
A plate full of courtly vegetables
is healing balm for the cells.
Cruciferous vegetables like
broccoli, kale, and cabbage, as
well as root vegetables like
carrots and beets are especially potent.
They fight inflammation, balance blood sugar and help ward
off chronic diseases.
GRATITUDE
Gratitude turns what we have into enough. It shifts our focus
from lack to abundance, and this reduces anxiety and causes
an increase in happiness.

title: MEDICINE WITHOUT MEDICATION
content:
Science confirms what faith has
long taught, that a grateful heart
leads to a healthy body.
Your daily expression of gratitude
can lower cortisol levels, improve
sleep, and enhance relationships.
FORGIVENESS
I bet you’re familiar with the statement, “unforgiveness is
like drinking poison and expecting someone else to suffer”.
I once heard a story of a man who was sick and had gone to
different hospitals but couldn't seem to get to the root of his
sickness, and then one day he meets a pastor who tells him
by word of knowledge that he seems to be angry with a
certain individual and even calls the individual’s name.
Immediately the man heard the person's name, his
countenance changed and he began to rain curses on the
individual.

title: MEDICINE WITHOUT MEDICATION
content:
Truly, this person had done something really inhumane to
this man, and he had every right to be angry, but he had been
angry with this person for up to ten years and had vowed
never to forgive him. I'm sure you can already guess the
origin of his sickness; it was holding on to such a heavy
grudge and pain for such a long time that had affected his
physical health.
Holding on to resentment can create toxic stress in the body.
Research has shown that chronic anger puts you into fight or
flight mode, which in turn results in numerous changes in
heart rate, blood pressure, and immune response. Those
changes then increase the risk of depression, heart disease
and diabetes, among many other conditions. Forgiveness on
the other hand, calms stress levels, releases the burden
bringing peace to the heart and healing to the body, boosts
the immune system, and even improves mental health.
The act of forgiveness can reap huge rewards for your health,
lowering the risk of heart attack; improving cholesterol levels
and sleep; and reducing pain, blood pressure and anxiety
levels, depression and stress. Research also points to an
increase in forgiveness-health connections as you age.
Unfortunately the man in our story refused to forgive and it
wasn’t long before his heart couldn't carry that load again
and it gave way. Just like that, he died an untimely death
while the person he was angry with was probably still alive.

title: MEDICINE WITHOUT MEDICATION
content:
You've probably heard this statement “forgiveness is first for
you before the offender.” and it rings true, no matter who you
are.
STUDYING GOD’S WORD
The Bible is more than just a book and this is something
you’ve probably heard a few times. There’s nothing you need
that can’t be found inside the pages of the Bible. There’s no
answer it doesn’t provide and no confusion it doesn’t clear
up. The Bible is a life-giving guide!
It is no secret that the Bible holds wisdom concerning every
single aspect of life including health and healthy living. I met
a friend who is a nutritionist and in her videos, she talks
about some of the food and plants/vegetables mentioned in
the Bible and their health benefits. You’ll be shocked to know
the amazing health benefits of some plants and vegetables
God commanded the children of Israel to eat.
This goes to show that God is and will always be interested in
our health. Studying God’s word doesn't just renew your
mind, it provides wisdom, and offers comfort in times of
distress. It also fosters a deep sense of purpose and peace,
helping you navigate life with hope and trust.

title: MEDICINE WITHOUT MEDICATION
content:
EATING RIGHT AND AT THE RIGHT TIME
I could write a whole book about this! It’s not just about what
you eat but also about when you eat it. The human body
functions at its best when it gets a refill of fuel every 3-5
working hours.
Whether you’re part of the people that wake up starving, or
you have little interest in food in the morning (though it’s
not a requirement for health to eat immediately upon waking
up), it is a good idea to eat something within 1-2 hours of
waking (except you’re fasting). This gives the body energy to
move and be active, and it provides the brain with the much
needed fuel to concentrate and learn.
Eating in the morning has also been shown to reduce
irritability and improve mood. I’m sure most, if not all of us,
can attest to the fact that eating puts us in a jovial mood, and
as the saying goes, a hungry man is an angry man. So when
you eat in the morning, it’s a win-win all around. That’s why
it’s the best idea to give the body most of its energy during
the day when you’re most active.
Once you consume your first meal, it’s natural and normal to
eat again within 3-5 hours, and then 3-5 hours after that and
so on for the rest of the day. Consistent meal timing supports
metabolism, hormone regulation, and digestion. Eating

title: MEDICINE WITHOUT MEDICATION
content:
whole balanced meals rich in fiber, healthy fats, and lean
proteins nourishes the body and helps maintain energy
throughout the day.
THINKING RIGHT
If you’re a Christian who knows the Bible, you’re probably
familiar with Proverbs 23:7 that says, ‘As a man thinketh in
his heart, so is he’ and I heard someone say ‘as he continues
to think, so he remains’. Even if you’re not a Christian I'm
sure you know that nothing changes until your mind
changes.
What others think about you is important, but what you
think about yourself is most important because your
thoughts shape your lifestyle. If you think highly of yourself
and value yourself, you will treat your body well because you
know you’re important, but if you don’t value yourself, you’ll
neglect every aspect of your life including your health.
Having a positive mindset towards life will lead to cultivating
healthy habits. If you ever come in contact with an optimist,
you will notice that one thing about them is they’re joyful
most of the time. This is because they view life from a glass
half full perspective rather than a half empty perspective. You
must understand that thoughts shape emotions and
emotions influence health.

title: MEDICINE WITHOUT MEDICATION
content:
This is why having a negative mindset is dangerous and
thinking right and positively is important, because negative
thinking can weaken the immune system and increase stress
hormones, while positive, faith-filled thoughts promote joy,
peace and healing. This is why cultivating a healthy thought
life is foundational to your holistic wellbeing.
TRUSTING AND BELIEVING GOD
This isn't a religious book, it’s a book written from years of
fact-checked experiences and science, so when I talk about
believing and trusting God as one of the medicines without
medications, then believe that it is exactly what I say it is.
Ever been to the hospital and heard the doctor tell you, a
loved one or maybe a stranger, that they couldn’t come up
with a diagnosis because they couldn’t find anything? This is
because some things are beyond medical or scientific
understanding. Some doctors even advise the patient to pray
and hope for a miracle especially if the case is something that
has gone out of hand.
HAVING TRUSTWORTHY FRIENDS
If you’ve never heard it said that community is the
cornerstone of health, you should take note of it today and
not trivialize community.

title: MEDICINE WITHOUT MEDICATION
content:
There are negative stories flying around about friends who
poison their friends to make them sick or even kill them, but
another narrative of friendship that isn’t talked about so
much is the narrative of trustworthy friends who help you
maintain a healthy lifestyle, who do not support unhealthy
habits, and who encourage you to be your best. Friends who
are there to provide support, encouragement and
accountability, who can hold your hand and walk with you
through difficult moments of depression and stress while
keeping the energy around you positive and faith filled.
Isolating yourself (which is what some people have chosen to
do) will do very little good and a lot of harm to you. It can lead
to depression and even physical decline, but building and
having healthy relationships nurtures the soul, and creates an
environment where all levels of healing can flourish.
DRINKING OF WATER
Ithink a large percentage of children and adults already
know that humans are made up of 70 percent water. It’s
common knowledge that everyone who has been to a
primary school has at their fingertips. It is also no news that
water is essential to life and to health. It’s been proven that
one can go without food for days and still survive as long as
they drink water, and that’s how essential water is.

title: MEDICINE WITHOUT MEDICATION
content:
Medically, we advise patients of all kinds, facing all kinds of
illnesses to consume water, and those who cannot take water
through their mouths are given IV fluids to prevent
dehydration and electrolyte imbalance.
Water helps in everything, from hydration, to detoxification,
to digestion, to temperature
regulation. Water helps in
the lubrication of joints, it
cushions the brain, water
helps carry nutrients to
cells and awhole lot of
other things! So the next
time you want to skip
drinking water because you
haven’t been thirsty all day,
think twice!
Your body needs water to
function and waiting till
you feel thirsty before drinking water is definitely not a good
idea. This is because although thirst is an important signal of
dehydration, it can sometimes be delayed, so choosing to rely
solely on the sensation of thirst can lead to insufficient
hydration, especially in situations like intense physical
activities or hot weather where water losses are high.

title: MEDICINE WITHOUT MEDICATION
content:
Now there are myths flying around like drinking large
amounts of water is best for your health, but the reality is,
while it is good to drink water, it’s more effective to hydrate
throughout the day with a moderate quantity of water rather
than taking in large quantities at a time because this will help
to maintain optimal balance throughout the day without
overloading the kidney.
Second, drinking too much water can be problematic because
it can lead to a condition known as hyponatremia which is
the dilution of electrolytes (sodium) in the blood.
The general recommendation for hydration is that healthy
adults drink around 8 glasses of water aday which is
equivalent to 2 litres, although individual needs may vary
depending on factors like climate, physical activities, health,
and age.
The important tip is to make sure to keep your body hydrated
at all times!
A PEACEFUL HEART
Peace is the ultimate medicine, as a heart at peace is not
easily shaken by life’s storms. Peace lowers stress, stabilizes
emotions, and creates ahealing environment within the
body. Of course, peace doesn’t come from perfect

title: MEDICINE WITHOUT MEDICATION
content:
circumstances, rather it comes from trust in God, gratitude
and complete surrender.
In conclusion, medicine without medication is not only
possible, it is powerful. It’s found in our choices, our
thoughts, our faith, and our relationships. These principles
do more than treat symptoms; they transform lives

once heard someone I respect greatly say, ‘If you study
the Bible closely, from the days of Adam to Noah, man’s
lifespan was at its peak even after the fall, and this is
largely because they ate plants and vegetables, not
meat.
Immediately there was an introduction of the eating of meat
after Noah, man’s life span began to shorten.’
While we might want to argue about the credibility or truth of
that statement, one fact that is credible and true according to
medical research is that the consumption of red meat has
been linked to several health issues which in turn leads to a
shortened life span.
Red meat can be an important source of protein, calories, and
Bvitamins. However, research suggests that red meat
consumption is also associated with health risks.
Detrimental effects of consumption of red meat include the
development of cardiovascular disease and cancer, which
leads to a shortened lifespan.

title: MEDICINE WITHOUT MEDICATION
content:
In Nigeria, the most consumed meat is red meat and it is so in
most countries around the world. Now, while some of us
might have heard about the dangers of consuming too much
red meat, and some people might not take it seriously, the
truth is that there is still ample evidence to suggest that red
meat can increase the risk of cardiovascular disease, cancer,
and overall mortality.
Long before the advent of pharmaceuticals, nature provided a
pharmacy of its own, a rich abundance of vegetables, fruits,
herbs, and oils that supported health and healing. These
gifts, many of which are mentioned in ancient texts and
scriptures, were not only staples of the diet of that time, but
also instruments of wellness. In this chapter, we will explore
these divine offerings, highlighting their components and
the medicinal benefits they carry, proving that God's
pharmacy is always open.
OLIVES
The olive tree is often called the Tree of Life. Olive oil,
particularly extra virgin olive oil, is packed with
monounsaturated fats and powerful antioxidants like
oleuropein and hydroxytyrosol. These compounds help
reduce inflammation, support cardiovascular health, and
even offer anti-cancer properties. The oil also enhances brain
function and protects against neurodegenerative diseases.

title: MEDICINE WITHOUT MEDICATION
content:
POMEGRANATES
Rich in vitamin C, potassium, and punicalagins (polyphenols
with strong antioxidant properties and anti-inflammatory
effects), pomegranates are among the most antioxidant-rich
fruits on earth. Their juice is known to reduce blood pressure,
improve cholesterol profiles, and support heart health.
Pomegranate seeds also have antimicrobial properties,
making them a natural immune booster.
WHEAT
Whole wheat is more than a carbohydrate. It’s a complex
source of Bvitamins, fibre, magnesium, and zinc. When
consumed in its unrefined form, wheat supports digestive
health, stabilizes blood sugar, and provides sustained energy.
It’s important, however, to choose organic and minimally
processed wheat to retain its medicinal integrity.
FIGS
Figs are a powerhouse of dietary fibre, potassium, calcium,
and natural sugars. They help in regulating blood pressure,
improving bone health, and relieving constipation. Figs also
contain antioxidants that support cellular repair and boost
immunity.

title: MEDICINE WITHOUT MEDICATION
content:
BARLEY
Barley is rich in beta-glucan, a type of soluble fibre known to
reduce cholesterol and balance blood sugar levels. It is also an
excellent source of selenium, magnesium, and B vitamins.
Barley water has been used for centuries as agentle
detoxifier and kidney cleanser.
GUINEA CORN AND MILLET
These ancient grains are gluten-free, high in protein, and rich
in iron, calcium, and dietary fibre. Guinea corn (sorghum)
supports cardiovascular health and helps manage diabetes.
Millet is known for its alkalizing properties, which help in
maintaining a healthy pH balance and reducing
inflammation.
GRAPES
Grapes contain resveratrol, a potent antioxidant that protects
the heart and slows the aging process. They also support
brain function, reduce inflammation, and help cleanse the
liver. The skin and seeds of grapes are especially therapeutic
when consumed whole.

title: General Health & Body Maintenance (Without Using Pharmaceutical Products)

content:
ver the course of the decades I spent in the practice of
medicine, where Iworked with patients from all
walks of life.
Young and old, urban and rural, rich and poor, I prescribed
countless medications, performed procedures, and made
diagnoses that changed lives.
I saw the wonders of modern medicine, how a tiny pill could
reduce blood pressure or how antibiotics could clear an
infection in days, and Ialso began to understand how
prevention, through a healthy lifestyle and food and herbs
would benefit every one of my patients and myself, far more
than curative exercises in the form of pharmaceuticals.
During my time at the bedside treating patients, I found
myself reflecting on the root causes of illness. I realized that
many of the conditions my patients presented with on a daily
basis were not merely biological accidents but, more often
than not, the consequences of their lifestyles: what they ate,
how they moved (or didn’t move), how much stress they
carried, how poorly they slept, and how disconnected they
had become from nature and their own bodies.

title: MEDICINE WITHOUT MEDICATION
content:
Now, with the gift of time and perspective, I see health
differently. I believe in science, and Ibelieve that
pharmaceuticals should not be our first line of defence. The
human body, as remarkably as God designed it, has the
innate ability to heal, maintain, and protect itself when we
allow it to do so. But in our modern world, where quick fixes
are constantly being sought after, we often silence that ability
with numbing pills, and habits that do more harm than good
for our bodies.
This chapter is a call to return to the basics, those simple,
often overlooked habits that keep our bodies resilient and our
minds at ease. It’s about eating real food, moving with intent,
sleeping deeply, breathing fully, and listening to the wisdom
our bodies quietly whisper every day. It’s about learning to
live with our bodies, not against them.
Here, I share insights from both my years in clinical practice
and my personal journey toward a more natural lifestyle. In
this chapter, Ishare timeless principles, supported by
experience and common sense, that can help you maintain
your health without using pharmaceuticals.
Let's explore together how you can take charge of your health
through the power of daily habits. Whether you're young or
aging gracefully, already dealing with chronic conditions or
simply seeking to prevent them, this chapter is for you.

title: MEDICINE WITHOUT MEDICATION
content:
Join me as we walk together down the path of natural
wellness. The goal is not perfection, but balance, vitality, and
a deeper connection to your own body.
UNDERSTANDING THE HUMAN
BODY’S SELF-HEALING POTENTIAL
Before we can fully embrace a lifestyle free from constant
pharmaceutical reliance, we must first acknowledge
something extraordinary: God designed the human body to
heal itself. In fact, much of modern medicine, even at its
most sophisticated, relies on the body’s natural healing
capacity.
Think about it this way: Doctors may stitch a wound, but it’s
the body that does the work to heal and close the wound. The
orthopaedic team sets a bone, but it’s the body that fuses it.
We can manage symptoms, but only the body can restore
balance from within.
In medical school, we were taught the concept of
homeostasis, that is, the body’s ability to maintain internal
stability despite external changes. This concept explains why
your heart rate rises when you exercise and slows when you

title: MEDICINE WITHOUT MEDICATION
content:
rest, why you sweat to cool down and shiver to warm up. It
explains the immune response to an infection, the
inflammation after an injury, and even the way your liver
neutralizes toxins you take in from your environment.
These mechanisms operate automatically, intelligently, and
with a biological wisdom that no medication can replicate.
But here’s the catch: the body can only optimally heal itself
when its natural processes are left alone to work without
interference.
Unfortunately, many modern habits interfere with the body's
healing function. Late-night scrolling disrupts circadian
rhythms. Ultra-processed foods burden our digestive systems
and feed inflammation. Our inactivity stagnates circulation
and compromises our metabolism. When the consequences
of our actions (or in actions) arise, we go to get quick fixes
from over the counter or we arm ourselves with prescriptions
rather than slowing down to ask what our bodies are telling
us.
Understanding the healing potential of our bodies starts with
listening to them. Aheadache might not be a call for a
painkiller, it might be a pointer to dehydration or stress.
Indigestion might not need an antacid; it might require
eating more mindfully or eliminating certain trigger foods.
These signals are not annoyances to silence; they are
messengers.

title: MEDICINE WITHOUT MEDICATION
content:
Here are some of the key systems that make self-healing
possible:
The Immune System: Your Natural Defence
The immune system is your first and most vital line of
defence. It fights off viruses, bacteria, and even abnormal
cells that could become cancerous. Awell-functioning
immune system adapts, remembers, and learns. But it also
needs nourishment in the form of real food (not empty
carbohydrates or ultra-processed foods), sufficient rest,
emotional calm, and minimal exposure to toxins.
Rather than “boosting” the immune system with synthetic
pills, we can support it by living in alignment with what our
body demands: clean air, clean water, sunlight, adequate
nutrition, and physical movement.
Inflammation
Inflammation has become quite the buzz word in addition to
getting a bad name, but in its acute form, it is essential for
normal functioning. When you sprain your ankle or cut your
skin, the inflammation that follows is part of healing. The
problem arises when inflammation becomes chronic (stays
for along time) often as a result of stress, poor diet, or
environmental toxins.

title: MEDICINE WITHOUT MEDICATION
content:
Pharmaceuticals can suppress inflammation without
addressing the root cause. But when we focus on reducing
internal stressors (by improving diet, managing emotions,
and avoiding exposure to toxic substances), we give the body
a chance to heal naturally.
The Nervous System
Your nervous system, particularly the parasympathetic
branch, is responsible for "rest and digest" functions. This is
the state in which healing occurs. Unfortunately, many of us
live in a constant state of sympathetic overdrive, the “fight or
flight mode” due to stress, overstimulation, and poor
boundaries.
Learning to regulate the nervous system through breathing,
meditation, prayer, or quiet time in nature can be more
powerful than any pill for conditions like anxiety, insomnia,
high blood pressure, and digestive upset.
The Body’s Feedback Mechanisms
Pain, fatigue, skin rashes, mood changes, and bloating are
not just symptoms to cover up. They are feedback
mechanisms activated by the body to alert us to imbalances
in its functioning. When we learn to decode rather than
suppress these mechanisms, we become active participants
in our own healing.

title: MEDICINE WITHOUT MEDICATION
content:
Think of your body as ahighly intelligent organism
constantly communicating with you. The question is: Are you
listening?
PILLARS OF NATURAL HEALTH
MAINTENANCE
The body is capable of healing itself, and our role is not to
micromanage or bombard this healing process with
chemicals and prescriptions, but to create the conditions in
which health can flourish. In my years of practice and
personal observation, I have found that those who remain
healthy without frequent reliance on medication have one
thing in common: they live in harmony with the basic
principles of human biology.
I call these principles the pillars of natural health
maintenance. Like the legs of a well-made table, they each
support your overall well-being. When one is neglected, the
entire system begins to wobble. But when they work
together, the body becomes strong, balanced, and resilient.
Here are some of these pillars.

title: MEDICINE WITHOUT MEDICATION
content:
Nutrition and Diet
Hippocrates, the father of Medicine, said “Let food be your
medicine, and medicine be your food”. This statement was
made centuries ago and it still rings true in these modern
times.
The food you eat does not just fill your belly, it nourishes
your cells, your immune system, and your hormones. It
either promotes healing or hinders it. In the pharmaceutical
model of care, food is often overlooked, but it is one of the
most powerful tools we have. How do we utilise our diet to
promote health and wellbeing?
Eat whole, natural foods
Avoid refined sugars.
Eat a diet focused on reducing inflammation. An example
is the Mediterranean diet which emphasized healthy fats.
Eat fermented foods to improve gut health. A healthy gut
is critical to a healthy body. Include fermented foods like
yogurt, kefir, and fermented locust beans (iru) in your diet.
These feed the microbiome (the trillions of beneficial
bacteria in your digestive system) that support digestion,
mood, and immunity.
Drink enough water
Employ natural supplements like Moringa, Spirulina,
Turmeric, and Vitamin D3

title: MEDICINE WITHOUT MEDICATION
content:
Physical Activity
The body was made to move. God knew what he was doing
when he designed it that way. Movement is not just for
weight loss. It is essential for circulation, lymphatic drainage,
mental health, bone density, and energy production. How can
you incorporate movement into your daily routine?
Move Every Day:
Walking briskly for
30–45 minutes aday,
dancing to your favorite
music, or doing simple
stretches can work
wonders. If you sit for
long hours, set a timer
and take movement
breaks every hour.
Incorporate variety into
your movements.
Some    examples
include:
- Cardiovascular exercise (walking, swimming, cycling)
improves heart health.
- Strength training (using body weight or resistance
bands) maintains muscle and bone mass.

title: MEDICINE WITHOUT MEDICATION
content:
- Flexibility and balance exercises (yoga, tai chi) reduce
injury risk and enhance mobility.
Sleep and Rest
In my practice, I encountered countless people who were
doing “everything right” but still felt exhausted. The missing
link was often rest.
Sleep is not a luxury; it is a biological necessity. During deep
sleep, the brain detoxifies, hormones reset, and tissues repair.
Chronic sleep deprivation contributes to weight gain, mood
disorders, lowered immunity, and even heart disease.
It is important to cultivate healthy sleep habits like:
- Sticking to a consistent sleep-wake schedule
- Limiting screen time before bed (blue light disrupts
melatonin production)
- Creating a cool, dark, quiet environment for sleep
- Avoiding heavy meals and stimulants in the evening
- Employing intentional rest (naps, quiet reflection,
prayer, or time in nature) which will allow the body to
shift into healing mode and the nervous system to
reset.
I have a tried-and-true natural method for enhancing sleep. I
just take a blended mixture of pineapple and watermelon and

title: MEDICINE WITHOUT MEDICATION
content:
it sends me right to sleep! No need for supplements or any
pills. You should try it and see.
Stress Management
You can eat the perfect diet and exercise daily, but if your life
is full of long-lasting stress, true health will be far from you.
Stress releases cortisol, a hormone that, when persistently
elevated, suppresses immunity, increases belly fat, disrupts
sleep, and contributes to anxiety and depression.
Stress can be managed naturally by employing the following
techniques:
Breathing exercises
Simple diaphragmatic breathing calms the nervous system
Mindfulness and meditation
Helps you stay grounded in the present
Spiritual practices
Prayer, reflection, meditation or reading the Bible can soothe
the soul. Jesus tells his followers to come unto him and
exchange their burdens with his, and they will find rest.
Time in nature
Even a 10-minute walk outdoors reduces stress markers
Creative outlets
Painting, music, gardening, or journaling provide emotional
release

title: MEDICINE WITHOUT MEDICATION
content:
Set Boundaries
Say no to what drains you. Learn to prioritize peace over
productivity when necessary. Your health depends on it.
Supporting the Body’s Natural Cleansing
Systems
One of the most over-marketed and misunderstood concepts
in health today is detoxification. On one end of the spectrum,
we see expensive teas, powders, and cleanses promoted as
miracle cures. On the other, we hear critics dismiss the whole
idea of detoxing as pseudoscience, claiming that the body
detoxifies itself.
As someone who has studied the human body in both illness
and recovery, let me offer a balanced perspective: Yes, the
body detoxifies itself, only when it is supported, not
burdened.
The liver, kidneys, lungs, skin, and digestive system all work
in harmony to filter and eliminate waste products from
metabolism, environmental toxins, and even stress
hormones. But the modern lifestyle can slow these systems
down, leading to a toxic backlog that may show up as fatigue,
brain fog, skin breakouts, hormonal imbalances, or recurring
infections.

title: MEDICINE WITHOUT MEDICATION
content:
The goal of detoxification is not to force or flush the body
with drastic interventions. It is to gently and consistently
support the organs responsible for cleansing. Let's explore
how we can support our body’s detoxification system (the
liver, kidneys, colon, lungs, and skin).
The Liver
The liver is your body’s detox powerhouse. It
breaks down toxins and packages them for safe
removal through bile or urine. However, it can
become overburdened by excess sugar and
alcohol, processed foods, prescription
medications, and environmental pollutants such as
pesticides, plastics, and fumes. You can support your liver
properly by:
- Eating cruciferous vegetables: Broccoli, cabbage,
cauliflower, and kale enhance liver enzyme activity.
- Drinking enough water: Water helps flush out the
byproducts of detoxification.
- Limiting alcohol and reducing medication
dependency where safe and appropriate.
The Kidneys
The kidneys filter about 50 gallons of
blood daily, removing waste through
urine. When overworked, which may be

title: MEDICINE WITHOUT MEDICATION
content:
due to dehydration, high salt intake, or a protein-heavy diet,
they can’t function efficiently. You can support the kidneys
by:
- Drinking clean water consistently throughout the day.
- Eating water-rich foods like cucumbers, watermelon,
citrus fruits.
- Reducing processed salt; use sea salt in moderation if
needed.
- Avoiding artificial sweeteners, which can stress the
kidneys over time.
The Colon
A sluggish colon leads to toxin reabsorption,
bloating, and even mood imbalances. Regular
bowel movements are essential for
detoxification.
To keep your colon moving, you should:
- Eat high-fibre foods: fruits, vegetables, oats, and
legumes.
- Add fermented foods and probiotics to your diet
because they support healthy gut flora for better
digestion and elimination.
- Stay active: Movement stimulates bowel motility
- Don’t ignore nature’s call: train your body to
eliminate regularly, preferably in the morning.
-

title: MEDICINE WITHOUT MEDICATION
content:
The Lungs
You exhale toxins with every breath. Shallow,
chest-level breathing limits this natural detox
route.
- Practice deep belly breathing daily,
especially in fresh air.
- Avoid indoor pollution: limit use of chemical cleaners,
air fresheners, and poorly ventilated spaces.
The Skin
Your skin eliminates toxins through sweat.
When blocked by synthetic cosmetics, heavy
creams, or lack of movement, it can become a
bottleneck.
Healthy Skin Practices:
My personal practice for a healthy skin is a combination of
Moringa leaves and aloe Vera blended together into paste
with yoghurt and vitamin C (1000 ml slow release), to be
taken at bedtime. This doesn’t just help give you a glowing
skin, it helps with blood level improvement and deals with
ulcer.
Some other regular healthy skin practices include:
- Sweating regularly: through exercise, steam baths, or
sauna (if accessible).

title: MEDICINE WITHOUT MEDICATION
content:
- Taking regular baths. Ensure that your skin is clean
- Using natural skincare: coconut oil, shea butter, and
plant-based soaps nourish without clogging.
- Wearing breathable clothing, especially in a climate
such as ours.
Natural Prevention of Common Ailments
Contrary to popular belief, we are not born to age into chronic
disease. Illness is not an inevitable part of living long. What
we call “common” ailments are often just the results of
common lifestyles of the age.
The good news is that just as unhealthy habits quietly invite
disease, healthy habits build a shield around the body and
help prevent disease. These simple, non-pharmaceutical
approaches can protect us from the conditions that have
sadly become too familiar in today’s world.
Heart Health Without Pills
Heart disease remains the leading cause of death globally, but
it is also one of the most preventable. Blood pressure,
cholesterol levels, and circulation are all highly responsive to
lifestyle changes.

title: MEDICINE WITHOUT MEDICATION
content:
Natural preventive strategies for heart disease include:
Reduce salt and processed foods: Excess sodium stiffens
blood vessels.
Embrace healthy fats: Avocados, nuts, seeds, olive oil, and
omega-3-rich fish (like sardines or mackerel) improve
cholesterol balance.
Daily physical activity: Walking, swimming, or dancing
helps regulate blood pressure and strengthens the heart
muscle.
Garlic and onions: These natural blood thinners improve
circulation and reduce clotting risk.
Hibiscus tea and beet juice: Both have been shown to
naturally lower blood pressure over time.
Blood Sugar Balance
Modern diets (which are rich in refined carbohydrates and
low in fiber) have made insulin resistance acommon
problem whereas the body was designed to manage blood
sugar efficiently when we eat in harmony with its rhythms.
Natural Blood Sugar Control Tips:
Eat balanced meals: Pair carbohydrates with healthy fats,
protein, and fiber to slow glucose absorption.
Avoid sugary drinks and snacks: Replace with water, herbal
teas, or fruit in moderation.

title: MEDICINE WITHOUT MEDICATION
content:
Cinnamon, bitter leaf, and fenugreek: These traditional
herbs and spices can improve insulin sensitivity.
Exercise regularly: Even short walks after meals help move
sugar from the blood into the muscles.
Intermittent fasting: With proper guidance, it can reset
insulin response and improve metabolic flexibility.
I have a personal recipe that can help keep you full for longer.

leaves, and fresh Sycamore leaves, filter the extract, bottle it
and keep it in the fridge. It helps keep me full and energised,
and you can try it too if you're going to hop on the
intermittent fasting train.
Above all, consistency is key. Small daily choices compound
and have long-term benefits.
Natural Immunity Building
Your immune system is not asingle organ but a whole
network that includes the skin, gut, white blood cells,
lymphatic system all working together to defend you. It
thrives on nourishment, rest, and apositive internal
environment.

title: MEDICINE WITHOUT MEDICATION
content:
Ways to Boost Immunity Without Medication:
Eat the rainbow: Colorful fruits and vegetables contain
immune-enhancing antioxidants.
Sunlight exposure: A natural way to maintain Vitamin D
levels, which are critical for immune response.
Probiotics and fermented foods: A healthy gut = a strong
immune system.
Adequate sleep: Less than 6 hours anight suppresses
immune cell activity.
Stress reduction: Chronic stress lowers immunity and delays
recovery.
Improving Digestive Health
Many people suffer from bloating, constipation, indigestion,
or acid reflux due to poor eating habits. But digestion is
central to health. You are not what you eat; you are what you
absorb.
Digestive Health Tips:
● Chew your food thoroughly: Digestion starts in the
mouth.
● Add natural digestive aids: Ginger, mint, pineapple,
and papaya contain enzymes that support digestion.
● Eat at regular times: Skipping meals or erratic eating
confuses your digestive rhythm.

title: MEDICINE WITHOUT MEDICATION
content:
● Stay upright after meals: Helps prevent reflux and
improves assimilation.
Regular elimination is
equally important. If
you're not passing
stool daily, your body is
retaining waste.
Hydration, fibre, and
movement are the best
remedies    to    a
backed-up colon.
Joint and Bone Health
Joint stiffness, arthritis, and bone loss are common ailments
of the aging or elderly, and are often treated with painkillers
or supplements. What if I told you that prevention of these
conditions lies in motion, nutrition, and mineral balance?
Keeping Joints and Bones Healthy Naturally:
Stay active: Movement lubricates joints and maintains
muscle support around them.

title: MEDICINE WITHOUT MEDICATION
content:
Eat calcium-rich foods: Green leafy vegetables, sesame seeds
(benniseed), and okra.
Vitamin D: Through sun exposure or food sources like eggs
and fish.
Add anti-inflammatory spices: Turmeric, ginger, and black
pepper can ease joint discomfort.
Avoid acidic and inflammatory foods: Excess meat, fried
foods, or soda can accelerate joint degeneration.
Weight-bearing exercises like walking or climbing stairs
also help build bone density without medication.
Mind-Body Connection and Mental
Wellness
It has taken modern medicine many decades to come to the
conclusion that the mind and body are inseparably linked.
What we think, feel, and believe affects our hormones,
immune system, and even our ability to recover from illness.
In my years of practice, I witnessed firsthand how patients
who nurtured a peaceful, hopeful, and purposeful mindset
recovered faster, lived longer, and enjoyed better quality of
life, even without heavy medication. On the other hand, those
burdened by chronic stress, resentment, or depression often
saw their physical health decline no matter how many
prescriptions they received.

title: MEDICINE WITHOUT MEDICATION
content:
To live a truly healthy life, we must give our inner life the
attention it deserves.
Let's start by examining the impact of stress on health. Stress
is not just an emotional state. It has biochemical
consequences. When we are chronically stressed, our bodies
remain in a constant state of fight-or-flight. Cortisol and
adrenaline flood the system, suppressing digestion,
immunity, sleep, and even reproductive health.
Common effects of unmanaged stress include: high blood
pressure, stomach ulcers and indigestion, sleep disturbances,
hormonal imbalances, weakened immune response, mood
swings and depression. You may eat well and exercise
faithfully, but if your life is filled with anxiety and tension,
your body cannot fully heal or thrive.
Mental peace is not the absence of challenges, but the
presence of inner resilience. Fortunately, if you don't have it
just yet, you can build it with intentional habits.
Natural Practices for Emotional Wellness
Daily meditation or prayer: Even 10 minutes a day can calm
the mind and regulate emotions.
Deep breathing exercises: Afew slow, conscious breaths
signal safety to the nervous system.

title: MEDICINE WITHOUT MEDICATION
content:
Journaling: Writing down your thoughts releases mental
clutter and brings clarity.
Nature walks: Time in nature reduces stress hormones and
improves mood.
Forgiveness and letting go: Holding on to anger is like
drinking poison and expecting someone else to suffer.
Limiting negative media: What you consume mentally
affects you as much as physical food.
As someone who has counselled many patients, I can tell you
that peace is medicine, and it is often free.
The Role of Social Connections
Humans are social beings. We heal faster when we feel
connected, seen, and loved. Loneliness, on the other hand,
has been linked to depression, heart disease, and even
reduced life expectancy.
I will expand more on this in the chapter on love, but here are
some tips for nurturing healthy relationships.
● Spend time with friends and family who uplift you.
● Join community groups, faith circles, or wellness
clubs.
● Express gratitude and appreciation regularly.
● Set boundaries with people who drain your energy.

title: MEDICINE WITHOUT MEDICATION
content:
● A hearty laugh with a friend can lower blood pressure
as effectively as some medications. The Bible
compares laughter to medicine, and states that a
broken spirit dries the bones. A warm hug can release
oxytocin, which is the body’s natural calming
hormone.
Be Mindful
Mindfulness is simply the practice of being present: fully
aware of your body, thoughts, emotions, and surroundings
without judgment. It has been shown to reduce
inflammation, lower stress, and improve overall well-being.
Here are some simple ways to live mindfully:
● Eat slowly and with attention. Notice the taste,
texture, and smell of your food.
● Observe your emotions without reacting immediately.
Pause before you respond.
● Start and end your day with stillness: say a prayer,
take a deep breath, or reflect on your day. Meditation
also works.
● Disconnect from digital distractions regularly to
reconnect with yourself.
When the mind is settled, the body follows. When the mind is
in turmoil, no herb, pill, or diet can bring lasting healing.

title: MEDICINE WITHOUT MEDICATION
content:
Purpose and Spiritual Well-Being
Health is not only about preventing disease; it’s about living
fully. People who have a sense of purpose tend to live longer,
healthier lives. This purpose could come from faith, family,
service, creativity, or a vision greater than oneself.
Spiritual well-being is central to physical health. Whether
through prayer, reflection, or acts of kindness, connecting to
something beyond the self can bring profound healing.
In my own life, retirement has not meant an end to purpose.
If anything, I have found more of it in teaching, writing,
mentoring, and sharing all I have learned, not just as a doctor,
but as a fellow traveler in this journey of life.
The mind, emotions, and spirit form the foundation upon
which physical health is built. If we neglect them, even the
best diets and routines fall short. But if we care for them, they
become powerful allies in our journey toward
medication-free vitality.

title: Love: The Greatest Of Them All

content:
Love for God: The Spiritual Foundation of Health
t the heart of human well-being lies a
deep and often overlooked truth:
the connection between spiritual health and
physical health.
Love for God, which is expressed through faith,
devotion, and daily communion, forms the spiritual
foundation upon which a life of wholeness can be built. For
the Christian, this love is not merely a feeling; it is a way of
life, a relationship that anchors the soul and nourishes the
body.
In the Gospel of Matthew, Jesus teaches that the greatest
commandment is this: “Love the Lord your God with all your
heart and with all your soul and with all your mind.”
(Matthew 22:37). This is not just a religious obligation, but an
invitation to participate in a relationship that brings healing,

title: MEDICINE WITHOUT MEDICATION
content:
peace, and clarity to every area of life. Loving God with all
your being fosters a sense of purpose and belonging that
extends far beyond the physical.
When one cultivates love for God, it naturally produces
spiritual fruit: peace, patience, joy, self-control, and kindness.
These fruits, described in Galatians 5:22-23, have tangible
effects on mental and physical health. A person who walks in
peace and joy is far less likely to suffer from chronic stress,
anxiety, or emotional burnout.
Medical science increasingly affirms what the faithful have
always known: spiritual practices contribute significantly to
overall health.
Prayer and worship have been shown to reduce cortisol
levels, the body’s primary stress hormone. High levels of
cortisol are associated with inflammation, high blood
pressure, and weakened immune response. But moments
spent in deep prayer, silent reflection, or heartfelt worship
have a calming effect on the nervous system. They create
mental stillness and emotional equilibrium. In this way,
spiritual connection becomes a kind of internal
medicine—natural, non-invasive, and profoundly effective.
Loving God is not a one-way expression; it is a response to
the overwhelming love that God has already poured out. “We
love because He first loved us” (1 John 4:19). When we

title: MEDICINE WITHOUT MEDICATION
content:
understand and internalize the unconditional nature of God’s
love, we find rest. We no longer strive anxiously for approval
or worth. This internal assurance has a direct impact on our
physical body by slowing our heartbeat, relaxing our
muscles, and freeing our minds from unnecessary fear.
The love of God brings wholeness because it touches every
part of our being. It gives strength during illness, hope in the
face of despair, and clarity when life seems chaotic. Those
who love God find that they are less isolated, more resilient,
and better equipped to navigate life’s storms without being
overwhelmed.
One of the greatest benefits of a life centred around the love
of God is the sense of purpose it provides. In loving God,
believers discover ahigher purpose—not just survival or
success, but service, growth, and eternal significance.
This spiritual orientation shifts our focus from external
achievements to internal transformation. It redirects energy
away from the pursuit of perfection and into the pursuit of
presence, being present with God, with others, and with
ourselves. And this presence, full of love and grace, is a
healing force.

title: MEDICINE WITHOUT MEDICATION
content:
Love for Self
In a world that often confuses self-love with
selfishness, it is important to reclaim the true
meaning of loving oneself.
Far from being self-centred or prideful, healthy
self-love is a recognition that we are God’s creation, that we
are fearfully and wonderfully made (Psalm 139:14).
To love oneself is to honour the work of God and care for the
vessel He has given us: our bodies, minds, and souls.
Jesus taught in Mark 12:31, “Love your neighbour as yourself.”
This simple yet profound command reveals that self-love is
not only permitted, it is expected and it sets the standard for
how we treat others. If we do not practice love, grace, and
patience with ourselves, it becomes difficult to offer those
gifts to others.
Loving oneself includes taking care of one’s body through
rest, good nutrition, physical activity, and proper hygiene.
But it also means cultivating mental and emotional
well-being, by practicing self-forgiveness, setting
boundaries, and learning to speak kindly to yourself. It is the
choice to treat yourself as someone worthy of love, not
because of your performance or perfection, but because of
your God-given value.

title: MEDICINE WITHOUT MEDICATION
content:
Scientific studies show that people who practice
self-compassion have lower levels of anxiety and depression,
and higher levels of resilience and optimism.
On the other hand, self-criticism, shame, and neglect often
lead to chronic stress, which negatively affects the immune
system, digestive health, and even heart function. When you
are constantly hard on yourself, your body remains in a
low-grade fight-or-flight state, which can wear you down
over time.
Learning to love yourself is ahealing journey. It means
confronting false beliefs about your worth and replacing
them with God’s truth. It means showing yourself the same
mercy and patience you would show a struggling friend. It
means understanding that you cannot pour from an empty
cup and that you must first be filled before you can flow into
the lives of others.
In loving yourself rightly, you become a better steward of the
life God has given you. You create space for peace, rest, and
joy to flourish, thus laying the groundwork for emotional
stability, physical health, and meaningful relationships.

title: MEDICINE WITHOUT MEDICATION
content:
Love for Family: The First Human Connection
From the moment we are born, family is our first context for
experiencing love. It is in the embrace of our parents or
guardians, the laughter of siblings, and the rhythms of home
life that we first learn what it means to give and receive
affection, to belong, and to trust. Family love lays the
emotional foundation for all future relationships and plays a
profound role in shaping our health across our lifespan.
Strong, loving family bonds are one of the most powerful
protective factors against mental and physical illness.
Numerous studies have found that people who report close,
supportive family relationships have lower rates of
depression, reduced levels of stress hormones, and even
longer lifespans.
Emotional safety at home contributes to healthy brain
development in children, fosters resilience in adults, and
provides comfort and stability in times of crisis.
On the other hand, chronic conflict, neglect, or emotional
distance in families can be harmful to health. Toxic family
dynamics are associated with increased risk of hypertension,
anxiety disorders, and immune system suppression. The

title: MEDICINE WITHOUT MEDICATION
content:
absence of familial love leaves a void that, if left unaddressed,
can lead to emotional isolation and a weakened sense of
self-worth.
But the good news is this: healing and restoration are
possible, even in broken families. Forgiveness, open
communication, and spiritual grace can rebuild bridges that
seemed permanently destroyed.
Choosing love in the family context is not always easy, but it
is always worth the effort, and the health benefits are both
immediate and long-term.
God designed the family as a multigenerational blessing.
Grandparents, parents, children, and grandchildren each
have a role to play in reinforcing identity, culture, and faith.
Love that flows between generations is especially powerful.
For older adults, maintaining strong ties with younger family
members helps reduce the risk of cognitive decline,
depression, and loneliness. For younger members, especially
children and teens, regular positive interaction with older
relatives contributes to emotional stability, moral grounding,
and a greater sense of security.
In fact, family traditions create a deep emotional imprint.
They offer predictability in a chaotic world and serve as

title: MEDICINE WITHOUT MEDICATION
content:
reminders that we are part of something greater than
ourselves.
One of the most radical expressions of love in the family is
forgiveness. Families are not perfect. Wounds,
misunderstandings, and unmet expectations are part of the
human experience. But holding on to resentment or
bitterness can damage both your spirit and your body.
Forgiveness has been shown to lower blood pressure, reduce
anxiety, and increase feelings of happiness and empathy. It
releases not just the person who hurt you, but you, the one
who has carried the pain. Jesus modelled this perfectly when
He forgave even those who crucified Him (Luke 23:34). In
doing so, He showed that love always chooses mercy over
vengeance, healing over punishment.
When illness comes, a loving family becomes an essential
part of the healing process. Whether it's helping with
medication, offering emotional encouragement, or simply
being present, the love of family members can significantly
improve recovery outcomes.
Patients who feel cared for by their families are more likely to
follow treatment plans, maintain hope, and fight for their
healing. In fact, studies have shown that recovery from
surgeries, major illnesses, and even chronic diseases is

title: MEDICINE WITHOUT MEDICATION
content:
accelerated when patients have asupportive and loving
family environment.
Love in Friendships and Social Relationships:
Building Strong Connections
While family may be our first experience of
love, friendship and broader social
relationships play a vital and continuing role
in our emotional and physical wellbeing. Humans are
inherently social beings, created not just for survival but for
connection, companionship, and community.
Love in friendships, especially those built on mutual trust,
respect, and loyalty, offers akind of nourishment that
sustains us through every stage of life.
Scripture is filled with examples of deep and meaningful
friendships. David and Jonathan, Ruth and Naomi, Paul and
Timothy, each of these relationships exemplifies love that is
selfless, supportive, and rooted in faith.
Proverbs 17:17 says,
“A friend loves at all times, and a brother is born for adversity.”
This verse reminds us that friends are not just social
companions; they are emotional anchors and sources of
strength.

title: MEDICINE WITHOUT MEDICATION
content:
A true friend rejoices in your victories, walks with you in
sorrow, and speaks truth into your life even when it's hard.
These kinds of relationships don’t just bring joy, they protect
your health. Numerous studies have found that people with
strong social ties have lower risks of chronic diseases,
experience less cognitive decline, and live longer.
Friendships offer emotional ventilation, accountability,
shared experiences, and abuffer against life’s hardships.
Whether it’s a simple conversation, shared laughter, or a word
of encouragement, these interactions release oxytocin, the
“love hormone” that lowers blood pressure and reduces
cortisol levels, the body's stress hormone.
Like any meaningful relationship, friendship requires
intentionality. In our busy, hyper-digital world, real
connection can easily be replaced by shallow interactions.
But investing time, energy, and vulnerability in friendships
pays incredible dividends for mental clarity, emotional
stability, and even physical resilience.
Call a friend. Go for a walk together. Share a meal. Pray with
and for each other. These small acts are actually healing
practices that can improve mood, boost immune function,
and reduce inflammation.
Friendships also serve as mirrors. They reflect both our
strengths and our blind spots, and when grounded in love,

title: MEDICINE WITHOUT MEDICATION
content:
they help us grow into better, healthier versions of ourselves.
They hold us accountable to our values and encourage us to
keep pursuing our goals.
Beyond individual friendships, there’s abroader social
context that supports health: community. This could be a
church group, a neighbourhood, a workplace team, or any
circle where people share common values and care for each
other. When people feel they belong, they are more likely to
thrive.
Churches and faith-based communities offer not only
spiritual nourishment but also emotional support, practical
help, and a sense of identity. The New Testament Church in
Acts is aprime example of this: they shared meals,
possessions, and prayers (Acts 2:42–47). Their lives were
deeply interwoven, and this collective love became a source
of strength and vitality.
Love, Healing, and Longevity:
The Science and Spirit of Wholeness
Throughout this chapter, we've explored the many
dimensions of love. Each form of love serves as a thread in
the tapestry of a healthy, meaningful life. Now, let us draw the
circle to its full close by reflecting on how love promotes

title: MEDICINE WITHOUT MEDICATION
content:
healing, wholeness, and longevity, not only in theory but in
the tangible experience of body, mind, and spirit.
At a biological level, love and emotional connection trigger a
cascade of beneficial chemical reactions in the body.
Oxytocin (the “bonding hormone” or “love hormone”) is
released during moments of physical affection, empathy,
prayer, and deep connection.
Oxytocin lowers blood pressure, reduces inflammation,
increases pain tolerance, improves wound healing, and
regulates stress and anxiety. Similarly, dopamine and
serotonin, neurotransmitters associated with joy and
contentment, surge when we experience love, gratitude, and
purpose.
These chemicals help regulate mood and support immune
health. On the contrary, chronic loneliness, bitterness,
resentment, or unprocessed grief flood the body with
cortisol, the stress hormone. Over time, high levels of cortisol
have been linked to weakened immunity, high blood
pressure, digestive issues, and even memory loss.
Simply put: love heals; isolation harms.
From a Christian perspective, healing begins in the heart of
God. Love is not merely an emotion; it is the essence of God
Himself (1 John 4:8). When we walk in relationship with God,

title: MEDICINE WITHOUT MEDICATION
content:
we are not just spiritually nourished, but emotionally and
even physically strengthened.
Jesus, during His earthly ministry, often paired physical
healing with expressions of love and forgiveness. To the
woman with the issue of blood, He said, “Daughter, your faith
has made you well; go in peace and be healed” (Mark 5:34).
His love restored not just her body, but her identity and
dignity. Faith provides hope, and hope is apowerful
medicine.
What would it look like to make love the organizing principle
of your life?
It would mean:
● Choosing forgiveness over holding grudges
● Prioritizing connection over competition
● Practicing gratitude over complaint
● Seeking reconciliation over revenge
● Valuing presence over performance
These daily choices gradually rewire the brain, relax the body,
and create an inner environment that fosters peace, healing,
and longevity.
It’s not about perfection, but direction. Small acts of love
carry immense weight. Love adds up; the effects build up in

title: MEDICINE WITHOUT MEDICATION
content:
your soul and body over time, and flow over to the people
around you.
LOVE AND LONGEVITY
Blue Zones (regions of the world with the
highest concentrations of people over a
hundred years old) reveal something
remarkable.
While diet and activity matter, what truly sets these people
apart is their relational and spiritual health. They live
surrounded by close family, embedded in strong
communities, and many practice daily spiritual rituals. They
experience purpose, connection, and love, and they live
longer, healthier lives as a result.
This aligns perfectly with Scripture. Proverbs 3:1-2 says,
“My son, do not forget my teaching, but let your heart keep my
commandments; for length of days and years of life and peace
they will add to you.”
The commandments of God are grounded in love and those
who keep them receive not only spiritual blessing but also
physical vitality.
In the end, love is more than a feeling. It is a divine force, a
healing agent, and the true measure of health. The apostle

title: MEDICINE WITHOUT MEDICATION
content:
Paul captured it best in 1 Corinthians 13:13: “And now these
three remain: faith, hope, and love. But the greatest of these is
love.” Love is the beginning and the end of our lives. It is the
breath of God that animates our souls, the bridge that
connects us to others, and the balm that heals the wounds of
body and spirit.
To live alife of love is to walk in harmony with God’s
design—for our health, our joy, and our eternity.
Love is, truly, the greatest of them all.

title: MEDICINE WITHOUT MEDICATION
content:
CONCLUSION
The wisdom contained in all the chapters of this book is a
function of my years of seeing patients from all walks of life
in different clinical settings, my years of study, and my
personal research and lived experiences.
It is my desire that you take to heart the words and wisdom
in this book and apply them to all the areas of your life to live
a life in which medications are only just a last resort.
A healthy life is essential to fulfil purpose and enjoy the life
that God has put you on the earth to enjoy. So, strive to
maintain health, and you will only have yourself, and God to
thank for it.
